review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an opinion that nowadays people's lives are heavily influenced by the news media and this is an adverse improvement. From my perspective, although it is not a positive development, this is not fully bad.

Admittedly, news media have too much influence on society these days. This can be seen clearly in the widespread access to smartphones and the Internet, which allow people to follow the news instantly regardless of wherever and whenever they are. It naturally follows that news has become a regular part of their routine. Another reason is the intense competition among news outlets. In order to gain attention, most media agencies focus on shocking and breaking content and present it in a highly sensationalized manner with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals, reinforcing the overall impact of news on public opinion.

Though this situation does not have only the negative effects. It is irrefutably true that the exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news will overwhelm people. This can also be possible to make them feel overly anxious and helpless even in situations that do not directly affect them. However, the news coverage these days also warn the public to existing and looming problems in society, say, crime, natural disasters, or political corruption. This helps individuals to be better informed and more prepared to respond to potential threats, making them be possible to handle risks in an increasingly complex society.
In conclusion, I strongly believe that although people are surrounding with news media today, it does not contain bad effects.

Admittedly, the news media exert a substantial influence on society today. This can be seen clearly in the widespread access to smartphones and the Internet, which allow people to follow the news instantly wherever and whenever they are. It naturally follows that news has become a regular part of their routine. Another reason is the intense competition among news outlets. review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: It is argued that schools should give rewards to students with the highest academic achievements, while others believe that recognizing personal improvement is more important. In my opinion, both approaches are necessary.

Admittedly, rewarding students with the top academic performances is genuinely true. As those students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve praise and privileges for their hard work. This recognition not only motivates these high achievers but also encourages others to study harder to win the rewards, ultimately propelling overall academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Due to it, students are used to this reality and learn to thrive in the face of fierce competition, enabling them to achieve greater success in their later lives.

However, rewarding those who show improvements is also important. If only a few exceptionally smart students can come first and receive rewards, it may cause others to feel that their efforts are futile. Realizing that they can not surpass those outstanding individuals, students who are less intelligent are prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened, gradually leading to losing their incentive to study. In contrast, emphasizing progress can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies. This approach helps students understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are currently performing. Eventually, the constant desire to outdo themselves can benefit students even more than the competitive determination to win against others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that schools should reward both students with excellent achievements and those who tried their best to improve in their studies.

Body 2 giải thích khá mạch lạc việc chỉ thưởng vài em có thể làm các em khác nản, rồi nối sang lợi ích của ghi nhận tiến bộ. Em còn gọi nhóm chưa đứng đầu là 'less intelligent' và khẳng định họ không thể vượt bạn; thành tích hiện tại không chứng minh hai điều đó. Em sửa theo từng chú thích, đặc biệt kiểm tra nguyên nhân–kết quả và mức độ khẳng định. Em có đủ hai lý do trong mỗi Body và dùng “Furthermore”, “In contrast” đúng chỗ cho ý thứ hai. paragraphs: It is argued that schools should give rewards to students with the highest academic achievements, while others believe that recognizing personal improvement is more important. In my opinion, both approaches are necessary.

Admittedly, rewarding students with the highest academic performance is justified. First, as those students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve praise and privileges for their hard work. This recognition not only motivates these high achievers but also encourages others to study harder to win the rewards, ultimately propelling overall academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. As a result of this competition, students are used to this reality and learn to thrive in the face of fierce competition, enabling them to achieve greater success in their later lives.

However, rewarding those who show improvements is also important. To begin with, if only a few exceptionally smart students can come first and receive rewards, it may cause others to feel that their efforts are futile. This is because other students may feel unable to surpass those high achievers. They may then feel overwhelmed and disheartened, causing them to gradually lose their incentive to study. In contrast, emphasizing progress can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies. This approach helps students understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are currently performing. In this way, the constant desire to outdo themselves can benefit students even more than the competitive determination to win against others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that schools should reward both students with excellent achievements and those who try their best to improve in their studies.

Some people think that school should reward students who show the best academic results, while others believe that it is more important to reward students who show improvements.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: These days some families have their children educated by their parents at home instead of letting them go to schools. Personally, I believe that the disadvantages it offers are much greater.

On the one hand, those who teach their children on their on way point to some advantages. This method allows parents to save money since no school fees are required. Home-educated children are also less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, which both cause emotional and mental problems. Furthermore, when parents teach their children at home by themselves, they can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones, which is often not the case in traditional schooling because of the large class size.

However, these things that the parents thought were not genuinely positive. This educational approach does not actually save money as parents need to pay a large amount of money for lab equipments and tutors. Moreover, one parent also needs to be cut off to cater for their child's needs, which contains both academic and personal ones. Additionally, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects, leading to difficulties in properly explaining concepts for children and ultimately academic problems. Even social problems that children could be faced with at school, say, bullying or having romantic feelings for others, also prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that children should go to school in person instead of following their parents' own education at home.
review.overall: Em hoàn thành bốn đoạn trên đúng một trang, nói rõ hại hơn và có đủ ba nhánh ở mỗi Body. Câu chủ đề 'those who teach their children on their on way' diễn đạt sai chủ thể và Body 2 gọi chung 'these things' nhưng chưa chỉ rõ lợi ích nào bị phản bác. Em có báo nhánh tài chính và chuyên môn bằng 'Moreover', 'Additionally', song chưa báo nhánh xã hội. Kết bài chuyển sang lời khuyên đi học trực tiếp, cần chốt phép cân lợi–hại của đề. Giữ các ý em đã viết, sửa quan hệ câu và từ dùng sai như 'lab equipments'.

paragraphs: These days, some families have their children educated by their parents at home instead of letting them go to school. Personally, I believe that the disadvantages of this approach are much greater than its advantages.

On the one hand, supporters of homeschooling point to several advantages. Initially, this method allows parents to save money since no school fees are required. In addition, home-educated children are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, both of which can cause emotional and mental problems. Furthermore, when parents teach their children at home themselves, they can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones, which is often not the case in traditional schooling owing to the large class size.

However, these apparent benefits are not entirely positive. Initially, this approach may not actually save money, as parents need to pay for lab equipment and tutors. One parent may also need to set aside working time to cater for the child's academic and personal needs. Additionally, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects, which can make it difficult to explain concepts to children properly and may cause academic problems. Finally, even social problems that children face at school, such as bullying and having romantic feelings for others, can prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that the disadvantages of homeschooling outweigh its advantages; therefore, children generally benefit more from attending school in person.

task.text: In some countries, parents are choosing to teach children themselves at home instead of sending them to school. Do the advantages of homeschooling outweigh the disadvantages?
